reason: I want to examine the channel grains, and collecting them in a sample jar is a natural first step.
expectation: I expect to collect a channel sample that I can examine more closely, though I don't know what it will contain.

alternatives.reason: The hammer also seems useful for exposing fresh rock, but I want to start with the channel sample.

effect: The jar collected channel sediment, so I can now examine it with the hand lens.
reaction: The result was straightforward; I’m curious what the grains will show.
reason: The hand lens is a natural way to inspect the collected sediment and work toward the channel goal.
expectation: I expect a closer view of the grains, though I don't know what features they will reveal.

alternatives.reason: Exposing the rock surface would also advance a goal, but I want to finish examining the channel sample first.

effect: The channel pebbles are rounder than the dry bank grains, suggesting wear and movement without identifying what carried them. The channel goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction between evidence of movement and its cause is interesting.
reason: The hammer is the only available combination and should advance the remaining goal of exposing fresh rock.
expectation: I expect to expose or collect a fresh surface from the layered ledge, though I don't know what it will reveal.

effect: The hammer produced a rock chip whose dusty face needs smoothing to reveal its internal grains.
reaction: The next step is clear, and I’m curious how the rock’s grains compare with the channel pebbles.
reason: The abrasive pad is the only available combination, and smoothing the chip should expose its grain arrangement.
expectation: I expect a smoother rock face that can be examined for its layers and grains.

effect: Smoothing the chip exposed curved fine bands around coarser grains and a pale vein crossing them, completing the rock goal. The result shows structure distinct from loose dust, though its history remains unclear.
reaction: The crossing vein makes me curious about how the rock formed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the channel sediment was most worthwhile because the comparison with angular dry-bank grains showed evidence of wear and movement while distinguishing that from knowing what carried them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting the channel sediment was a straightforward preparatory action with little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The fresh rock face revealed a pale vein crossing bands that curve around coarser grains; I had not expected that combination of features.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. Collecting and inspecting sediment, then chipping and smoothing rock, each had a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to learn what further evidence reveals about the channel and the layered rock, especially given the care taken not to claim a cause from rounded grains alone.
